title: "They Said It Was God... But It Was Control."
paragraphs:
"They Said It Was God... But It Was Control."
How to Recognize Spiritual Manipulation Before It Destroys Your Faith, Your Family, and Your Relationship with Jesus Christ
There is a kind of wound that does not bleed.
Yet it quietly steals something far more precious than money or time—it steals people's ability to hear the true voice of God.
Some people have walked away from church because of spiritual manipulation.
Some cannot even pray without hearing the voices of those who once claimed to speak for God.
This article is not here to condemn you.
It is here to remind you that Jesus never manipulates the people He came to save.
From the beginning, Satan has never needed to remove God's Word.
He only needed to twist it.
That was his strategy in Eden.
The attack was never against God's existence.
The devil wanted Eve to question whether God was truly good.
Spiritual manipulation still works exactly the same way.
It does not always deny Scripture.
It removes Scripture from its context until God's loving voice begins sounding like human control.
This is why knowing the Bible for yourself matters.
Because Scripture ultimately points to Him.
"You search the Scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life; and it is they that bear witness about Me." (John 5:39, ESV)
The Greek word translated "bear witness" is μαρτυροῦσαι (marturousai)—to testify, to give evidence.
Every page ultimately testifies about Christ.
When Scripture stops leading people toward Christ and instead leads them toward fear, dependency on personalities, or human power, something has gone terribly wrong.
One of the greatest examples appears in the ministry of Jesus Himself.
The religious leaders possessed astonishing biblical knowledge.
Yet they rejected the very Messiah those Scriptures announced.
"They tie up heavy burdens, hard to bear, and lay them on people's shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to move them with their finger." (Matthew 23:4)
He condemned religious burdens that God never required.
The Greek word φορτία (phortia) means heavy loads or crushing burdens.
Jesus then offered one of the most beautiful invitations in all Scripture:
"Come to Me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest."
Δεῦτε πρός με πάντες οἱ κοπιῶντες καὶ πεφορτισμένοι...
The word πεφορτισμένοι (pephortismenoi) literally describes people overloaded, weighed down, exhausted by crushing burdens.
His invitation was radically different from the religious culture surrounding Him.
"Come to Me because I will control every decision you make."
"Take My yoke upon you... for My yoke is easy, and My burden is light." (Matthew 11:28–30)
The Greek word χρηστός (chrēstos), translated "easy," means kind, gracious, fitting, beneficial.
That alone exposes countless forms of spiritual manipulation.
Spiritual manipulation often disguises itself as spiritual maturity.
"If you question me, you're questioning God."
"If you leave this ministry, you're leaving God's will."
"You cannot hear God unless you hear Him through me."
Even the Apostle Paul encouraged believers to examine what they were taught.
"They received the word with all eagerness, examining the Scriptures daily to see if these things were so." (Acts 17:11)
The Greek word ἀνακρίνοντες (anakrinontes) means to examine carefully, investigate thoroughly, evaluate honestly.
Paul did not fear people checking his teaching.
Healthy shepherds point people toward Christ.
Healthy pastors rejoice when believers know Scripture deeply.
Manipulators become threatened when people ask respectful questions.
Peter, one of Jesus' closest disciples, understood this profoundly.
"Shepherd the flock of God that is among you... not domineering over those in your charge, but being examples to the flock." (1 Peter 5:2–3)
The Greek word κατακυριεύοντες (katakurieuontes) means exercising oppressive control, ruling over people harshly, lording authority over them.
Peter did not merely discourage domination.
Jesus Himself made this distinction unmistakably.
"You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them... It shall not be so among you." (Matthew 20:25–26)
The kingdom of God is upside down compared to the kingdoms of this world.
The greatest servant becomes the greatest leader.
The greatest leader becomes the greatest servant.
Whenever spiritual authority becomes obsessed with power instead of service, Christ's model has already been abandoned.
Perhaps one of the clearest warning signs of manipulation is fear.
Afraid to study Scripture without permission.
"There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear." (1 John 4:18)
The Greek expression ἡ τελεία ἀγάπη (hē teleia agapē) refers to mature, complete, perfected love.
Some reading this carry deep scars.
Maybe someone quoted Romans 13 to demand unquestioning submission.
Maybe Hebrews 13:17 was used to silence concerns.
Maybe "touch not the Lord's anointed" was repeated whenever accountability became necessary, even though that phrase is frequently misapplied in modern contexts.
Perhaps Scripture itself now feels unsafe because someone misused it against you.
The problem was never God's Word.
The problem was sinful people using God's Word contrary to God's intent.
Even Satan quoted Scripture to Jesus during the temptation in the wilderness (Matthew 4:6).
He corrected its misuse with Scripture rightly understood.
"Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved... rightly handling the word of truth." (2 Timothy 2:15)
The Greek phrase ὀρθοτομοῦντα τὸν λόγον τῆς ἀληθείας (orthotomounta ton logon tēs alētheias) literally means "cutting straight the word of truth."
God never intended His Word to become a weapon of domination.
He gave it as a lamp to our feet and a light to our path (Psalm 119:105).
The Hebrew word for "lamp" is נֵר (nēr)—a guiding light for one's steps.
The Gospel itself dismantles manipulation because the Gospel continually points away from human performance and toward Christ's finished work.
When Jesus cried from the cross,
This single Greek word carries astonishing depth.
Nothing needs to be added to Christ's saving work.
No human leader can complete what Jesus has already completed.
No ministry can replace the grace Christ freely gives.
No personality can stand between the believer and the Savior.
"For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus." (1 Timothy 2:5)
That truth protects every believer from spiritual abuse.
Because your ultimate allegiance belongs to Jesus Christ.
If you have experienced spiritual manipulation, do not let the counterfeit keep you from the genuine.
Counterfeit money exists because real money exists.
False shepherds exist because the Chief Shepherd is real.
Perhaps the deepest scandal is not that spiritual manipulation exists.
The greatest scandal is that sinful humanity crucified the only perfectly loving Shepherd who ever lived.
Yet from that greatest scandal came the greatest grace the world has ever known.
The empty tomb forever declares that evil never has the final word.
God's Word, read in its context and centred on Christ, remains a trustworthy light.
Because one article can change a mind, one share can reach a soul, one testimony can restore hope, and one faithful act of obedience can become part of God's eternal work in someone's life.
Sometimes the voice you've been afraid to question was never God's voice at all—it was the echo of someone standing between you and the Shepherd who has been calling your name all along.
